overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by approving eight May minutes more than 30 days late and by omitting appointment candidates' names from the June 26 notice; June 5 onward minutes were not reviewed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to approve its May 5 through May 31 meeting minutes in a timely manner, approving them on July 10.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board reviewed and approved them more than 30 days after each meeting, on July 10, it did not approve them in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complaint concerned minutes of meetings from June 5 onward, which the Board had not yet approved when the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to review any of the minutes for meetings held on and after June 5 as the Board still had time to timely approve those minutes and, indeed, did so in most instances.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the June 26 meeting notice failed to list the names of individuals to be considered for appointment to town boards and committees.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the meeting notice should have included the names of the individuals being interviewed and/or considered by the Board

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
